title: Show HN: Documenting the file formats and engine of Elder Scrolls: Redguard 1998

item.title: Show HN: Documenting the file formats and engine of Elder Scrolls: Redguard 1998

sources.text:
Redguard Preservation
Reference documentation for
The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard
(1998) file formats, engine behavior, and undocumented features. The documentation covers the GOG release’s Glide renderer and notes known original-CD differences.
Reference sections
Engine behavior
: scripting, actor animation, movement, rendering, audio, menus, and hidden cheats.
File formats
: binary layouts for models, maps, textures, sound, saved state, and bundled support files.
Configuration
: INI settings for worlds, combat, items, input, rendering, and menus.
Look and feel
Reproducing the look and feel
explains how terrain
and model lighting, fog, sky, water, texture animation, camera projection, and
on-screen presentation combine, with links to each subsystem.

Engine lineage
Redguard runs on Bethesda’s XnGine, a DOS-based 3D engine. Battlespire used its own build of the engine, and Redguard added 3dfx Glide support.

Terminator and Daggerfall files share structure with Redguard’s:
Format
Shared structure
WLD terrain
The Terminator games use the same section layout and the same 128-entry height lookup table. Daggerfall’s
WOODS.WLD
uses the same container: width and height at
0x04
and
0x08
, an offset list at
0x90
, and a 22-byte header on each offset’s block. It stores 1000×500 cells and a 1000×500 elevation map.
3D models
Terminator and Daggerfall
.3D
files place the vertex block at
0x30
and the face array at
0x3C
. In
v2.6
and
v2.7
files the face texture field splits into an archive number (
value >> 7
) and a record number (
value & 0x7F
) in all three games.
Software texture banks
Terminator
TEXTURE.NNN
banks use the same 20-byte directory starting at byte 26. Image width, height, data offset, frame count, and frame delay sit at the same offsets, and animated frames use the same transparent-run and literal-run row encoding.
Terminator scenes use a cell grid with linked entity lists, not RGM sections.

Asset and support-file roles
Models, textures, fonts, UI images, maps, dialogue, sound effects, movie data,
and CD music supply the content of a faithful reimplementation. Hardware
configuration, audio-utility launch settings, SideWinder presets, and tool
reports describe the original environment. Their layouts remain part of the
format references in
Bundled support resources
.
The cursor file
system/pointers.bmp
contains a GXA archive despite its
extension.

and
fxart/fxart3dc.txt
are historical directory
listings, and
fxart/LOGFILE.TXT
records collision-sphere generation.
The support-file reference
describes these
files and the Miles setup catalog
sound/MSSDRVR.LST
.
Save-game containers
describe
SAVEGAME.SAV
and the
per-world
.TSG
snapshots. A slot’s
LOGBOOK.TXT
is journal content.
GOG vs original CD differences
The English CD installer contains software and Glide resources. GOG selects the
Glide distribution and omits the software-specific asset directory and executable.
The game data, renderer choice, configuration defaults, and host packaging
are separate parts of edition compatibility.

The CD places the DOS executables outside
DATA1.CAB

alone does not produce a runnable installation.

The directories overlap in model names, but are not interchangeable copies.
Glide includes additional standalone models; software includes additional ROB
archives. Even matching names can have different geometry and animation data:
TIRBA001.3DC
has different face and frame counts, and
NCROCK.3D
has different
face counts. Resolve resources within the chosen renderer’s asset set rather
than substituting a same-named file from the other set.
Both model generations use renderer-specific headers and texture references.
See

3dart/
contains 18 COL palettes, including
art_pal.col
, world palettes,
and sky palettes. It does not use
art_pal.col
exclusively. Matching palette
names can differ between renderers:
NECRO2.COL
and
REDGUARD.COL

contents. The Glide set contains 27 populated COL palettes and an empty
CLDTEST.COL
placeholder. See

Shared content
The English CD installer payload and GOG share byte-identical:
RGM scenes and their embedded scripts, WLD terrain, and PVO visibility data;
SOUP386.DEF
,
WORLD.INI
,
COMBAT.INI
,
ITEM.INI
,
MENU.INI
,
KEYS.INI
,
REGISTRY.INI
, and
surface.ini
;
ENGLISH.RTX
dialogue and speech,
MAIN.SFX
, and the other sound resources
except the configured
dig.ini
and
mdi.ini
device selections;
fonts and system artwork, including title, menu, HUD, and sky images.
Renderer-specific model and texture differences therefore coexist with shared
authored scenes, scripts, and presentation resources.

The CD cabinet’s
sound/dig.ini
and
sound/mdi.ini
contain setup comments
without device selections. GOG supplies Sound Blaster device and driver settings.
Hardware configuration belongs to the installation environment; it does not
replace the game’s Red Book music tracks.
Cinematics, disc audio, and support files
The CD Smacker movies are byte-identical to those in GOG’s data track,
including their embedded audio. GOG’s virtual disc omits the CD’s installer
cabinet, DOS engines, setup files, and bundled hardware-driver installers.
Its ISO9660 filenames
FINDRE~1.EXE
and
REDGUA~1.ICO
refer to the same
contents as the CD’s
FindRedguard.exe
and
RedguardCD.ICO
.
An extracted CD data directory contains movies and installation files, but
not the Red Book audio tracks. Mounting that directory as a CD-ROM cannot
reconstruct the missing music tracks. A music-capable disc source must retain
the audio tracks and their numbering; separately distributed soundtrack files
are not a substitute for the disc’s track layout. See
background music
.
GOG adds host Glide libraries and DOSBox launch configuration. The selected
Glide implementation determines the splash variant independently of the shared
Glide executable. See
startup presentation
.
